photos.caption: NASA's video, clock 14:45:50
photos.how: Frame from NASA's video at 2390 s; on-screen clock 04/06/13 14:45:50, wanted 14:45:50 (within 20 s; the matrix time plus one day). NASA's as-run matrix gives this test's start as '13-095: 14:45' on 2013-04-05 (`as run matrix!B90`), read as 2013-04-05 14:45. The video's on-screen clock reads one day later than the matrix on every day both cover, the same kind of offset NASA states for this clock on BASS-II, so the clock was searched for 2013-04-05 plus one day, 14:45: it was found 2340 s into this video, and in no other video. The fan setting on screen (68) is one the matrix's fan cell gives ('68, 51,  slowly to zero', `as run matrix!J90`).

findings.quote: Flame sequence of a burning 2-cm diameter acrylic sphere at 17 percent oxygen and 12 cm/s flow from the Burning and Suppression of Solids experiment. The images are about 1.5 sec. apart. With the reduction in oxygen from 21 percent (air) to 17 percent, the flame stays bluer much longer (soot formation is delayed) facilitating comparison with model.
findings.about: At 17% oxygen a burning acrylic sphere stays blue longer (soot is delayed)
findings.note: Caption of the Guide's Figure 11: a 2-cm diameter acrylic sphere at 17 percent oxygen and 12 cm/s. Tied to Test 99 by the SI tool's reading of the as-run matrix: only Tests 98 and 99 (sample 24, "PMMA 2 cm", 17.07% O2, Air display 12) fit, and Test 98's comment says "All still frames black because lens cap still on".
